chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who goes to his slave girl during the day in the month of Ramadan while traveling. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This one does not know the right of the month of Ramadan. For him, during the night, is a long duration (for rest/recovery).'

key_terms.سَبْحًا: Swimming/Resting (metaphor for long duration of rest)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man having intercourse with his slave girl during the day in Ramadan while traveling?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam (peace be upon him) addresses the specific case of a man engaging in sexual intercourse with his slave girl during the daytime of Ramadan while traveling. He critiques the man for not recognizing the true sanctity of the month, implying that the night is reserved for extended worship (*sahb* or *suhur*-like devotion) and spiritual elevation, whereas daytime intimacy, particularly in the context of travel or lesser reverence, reflects a neglect of Ramadan's higher spiritual potential. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the physical act and the spiritual consciousness required during the holy month.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who went to his slave girl during a Month of Ramazan, by the daytime, during the journey. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This one does not understand the right of a Month of Ramazan. For him, during the night, is a lengthy duration’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who experiences sexual relation with his slave-girl on a journey in the month of Ramadan during the day. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has not recognized any respect for the month of Ramadan even though there is a long time during the night.’” NOTE: Al-Kulayniy has said that it is better for one to pay respect to the month of Ramadan and abstain from sexual relation during the day. However, if one is overpowered by lust and is afraid from his soul in which case it is permissible to have what is lawful. It is as is permissible for a traveler who does not find water, when desire overpowers him, to have what is lawful. He has said that one receives rewards for it just as it is a sin when he commits something unlawful.
